commit.subject: [hlsl] Polyfill subgroup_id and num_subgroups
commit.message:
[hlsl] Polyfill subgroup_id and num_subgroups

If the workgroup size is linear, we can determine these values from
the location invocation index, the subgroup size, and the workgroup
size.

Otherwise, use an atomic workgroup counter that is incremented by each
subgroup to determine the the ID, and then broadcast that to every
other invocation in the subgroup. The number of subgroups is then the
final value in that counter.

Bug: 454652006
Change-Id: Ide6e51830b93674f1a6c15951244f8e0aebbb32e

commit.message:
Disable Toggle::D3D11DelayFlushToGPU for Qualcomm by default

Qualcomm 8380 device hangs randomly while running dawn end2end tests
with Toggle::D3D11DelayFlushToGPU enabled. So we disable this toggle by
default and skip all the related test cases with this toggle on.

commit.subject: Ignore Toggle::D3D11DelayFlushToGPU for Qualcomm
commit.message:
Ignore Toggle::D3D11DelayFlushToGPU for Qualcomm

Qualcomm 8380 device hangs randomly while running dawn end2end tests
with Toggle::D3D11DelayFlushToGPU enabled. Let's ignore this toggle on
Qualcomm until driver fixes this issue.
The toggle is ignored instead of disabled because many dawn end2end
tests force the toggle (d3d11_delay_flush_to_gpu).

commit.subject: tint/hlsl: add ArrayOffsetFromUniform transform
commit.message:
tint/hlsl: add ArrayOffsetFromUniform transform

ArrayOffsetFromUniform is a transform that adds an offset to storage
buffer loads and stores provided via a uniform buffer.

This will be used by the D3D12 backend to optimize root signature slot
usage. Instead of binding dynamic storage buffers to root decriptors at
the input dynamic offsets, these buffers will be bound in the root
descriptor table, and the input dynamic offset stored in root constants.
These offsets need to now be applied in the HLSL shader instead using
this transform in a way very similar to ArrayLengthFromUniform.

After this lands, I'll land the Dawn D3D12 backend changes that use this
transform.

Bug: 449703736
Change-Id: I19fb261070fecdccaa47323594ac2cec943fde63

commit.subject: [null] Add a simple Null backend to Tint.
commit.message:
[null] Add a simple Null backend to Tint.

This CL adds a `Null` backend which just runs SingleEntryPoint and
SubstituteOverrides and then returns the resulting workgroup
information. It is used by the `DeviceNull` backend in Dawn removing
the need to call the transforms directly. This makes `DeviceNull` behave
in a fashion similar to the other devices.

Change-Id: I80ca8ac1831f877198ec5ab51cfed6c2041f36b3

[ir] Reject binding_array in invalid address space

capability for putting them in structures is enabled (which is used by
MSL when putting them in argument buffers).

commit.subject: Refactor BufferBase
commit.message:
Refactor BufferBase

1. Change FinalizeMapImpl() to take |newState| as a parameter. This
   allows changing mState after FinalizeMapImpl() runs once the map
   operation has completed rather than before it completes.
2. Change UnmapImpl() signature to take |oldState| as a parameter. This
   doesn't matter now but it matches FinalizeMapImpl(). Also if later CL
   to transition state to InsideOperation lands we won't be able to use
   GetState() to know if the previous state was PendingMap vs Mapped vs
   MappedAtCreation so it must be passed as a parameter.
3. Combine UnmapInternal() calls from DestroyImpl() for clarity.

commit.subject: Refactor BufferBase
commit.message:
Refactor BufferBase

1. Change FinalizeMapImpl() to take |newState| as a parameter. This
   allows changing mState after FinalizeMapImpl() runs once the map
   operation has completed rather than before it completes.
2. Change UnmapImpl() signature to take |oldState| as a parameter. This
   doesn't matter now but it matches FinalizeMapImpl(). Also if later CL
   to transition state to InsideOperation lands we won't be able to use
   GetState() to know if the previous state was PendingMap vs Mapped vs
   MappedAtCreation so it must be passed as a parameter.
3. Combine UnmapInternal() calls from DestroyImpl() for clarity.
4. Remove assert that MapMode(), MapSize() and MapOffset() are only
   called if state is Mapped or MappedAtCreation. Since they are called
   from FinalizeMapImpl() the state isn't updated yet.

Bug: 425472913
Change-Id: I684cefc9ce88a2984658f05c93e8018c74ebfa53

commit.subject: [tint][uniformity] ignores post-loop code if loop only returns
commit.message:
[tint][uniformity] ignores post-loop code if loop only returns

Consider:

  loop {
    return;
    continuing { break if true; }
  }
  post_loop_code();

The loop behaviour is exactly {Return}, and so uniformity issues
in post_loop_code() should be ignored.

The short-circuiting of the analysis applies to all kinds of loops:
loop, for, and while.

While loops always have conditions, and so the behaviour of a while
loop always includes Next.

Similarly, a for loop with a non-empty condition clause will
have a behaviour including Next.

Fixed: 452692768
Change-Id: I6a6a6964630ea42948e308d037dbe75524289c5d

commit.subject: Enable Win/x64/GTX 1660 tests
commit.message:
Enable Win/x64/GTX 1660 tests

Enables tests on the Win/x64/NVIDIA GTX 1660 tester that are equivalent
to the ones run on the Chromium equivalent.

As a result, sharding is increased on all platforms to account for
slower tests on Windows without needing to use test_suite_exceptions.pyl
and the existing test bundle is renamed to include "common" since there
are some Windows-specific variants of the tests.

Bug: 452406604
Change-Id: Ib0a3517e4f15ca986501ba550d17639020927bee

commit.subject: [emscripten] Enable building with Closure Compiler when possible
commit.message:
[emscripten] Enable building with Closure Compiler when possible

We want to always build with Closure because it provides static analysis
checks that will catch some bugs in the bindings. However, Mac bots
can't run Closure (it requires either Rosetta 2 or Java), so detect this
situation and disable Closure in that case in GN.

Bug: 450959456
Change-Id: I423b8506e5636f215574312d3155327b3be6a298

commit.subject: [docs] Update documentation around Fuzzers on MacOS
commit.message:
[docs] Update documentation around Fuzzers on MacOS

The previously listed workaround for getting Fuzzers to work on MacOS no longer
appears to work with ToT Dawn + current XCode. But it does appear that the
fuzzers do build fine using the gn based build.

I have updated the documentation to indicate that gn based builds are
recommended here, and included some details of failing workarounds and one
working workaround for CMake builds, since certain dev setups do depend on the
CMake based builds.

Change-Id: I8ef3179bd0a98e266695b416e9d288d81d1e7746

commit.subject: Fix: WGPUBuffer getMappedRange with WGPU_WHOLE_MAP_SIZE
commit.message:
Fix: WGPUBuffer getMappedRange with WGPU_WHOLE_MAP_SIZE

When calling `wgpuBufferGetMappedRange` with `WGPU_WHOLE_MAP_SIZE`, the size of the returned mapped range should be the size of the buffer minus the offset.

This commit fixes the issue by:
- Updating the generator to handle `WGPU_WHOLE_MAP_SIZE` for `WGPUBuffer` in `methods.cpp`.
- Adding new tests in `BufferTest.kt` to verify the behavior of `getMappedRange` and `getConstMappedRange` with default and explicit offset/size values, including when `WGPU_WHOLE_MAP_SIZE` is used.

Bug: b/450476328
Change-Id: I8c2f78474cde441ca3bcaf8185f134b1fb4425cb

commit.subject: Kotlin: don't wrap Future, WaitStatus or other async related entities.
commit.message:
Kotlin: don't wrap Future, WaitStatus or other async related entities.

We supply a callback interface and coroutine adapter designed for
Kotlin apps. The remaining entities are present in dawn.json but not useful
for Kotlin, so likely just to confuse.

Test: ./gradlew connectedAndroidTest
Bug: b/446603126
Change-Id: Id7726e9f1189273da37a85357fc4a52fb8831cf4

commit.subject: Fix parsing of a semicolon before a break-if.
commit.message:
Fix parsing of a semicolon before a break-if.

When parsing a `continuing` statement we handle the `break-if` parsing
specially so it doesn't collide with the general `break` parsing. To do
so, we check explicitly and then if it doesn't match we hand off to the
statement parsing.

In the statement parsing a `;` by itself is ignored. This means we can
accidentally jump over the `break-if` parsing with a `;`, land in the
statement parsing and mistake the `break-if` for a break and error that
the `break` is missing a `;`.

Fix this by skipping `;` in the continuing code before checking if we
have a `break-if`.

Fixed: 453961764
Change-Id: I02b209d9994df17d5f65e8432269473bd2ef60ea

commit.subject: [ir] Remove recursion from Validator::CheckType
commit.message:
[ir] Remove recursion from Validator::CheckType

This shouldn't be needed as we already traverse into nested types with
a non-recursive walk. It also means we are validating types without
knowledge of their original `root` type, which is needed in some
cases.

Change-Id: If139366700bba7cb00857938fa757375c24d1e55

commit.subject: [ir] Validate struct size instead of asserting
commit.message:
[ir] Validate struct size instead of asserting

The assert can trigger when the struct alignment causes the size to
overflow a u32. Instead of asserting or trying to replicate all of the
logic for computing the size, just reject any struct that doesn't
satisfy the condition.

Fixed: 452981140
Change-Id: I8b450175e261561a8af15fab51f381b8caab4058

commit.subject: [glsl] Use DecomposeUniformAccess instead of Std140
commit.message:
[glsl] Use DecomposeUniformAccess instead of Std140

This prepares the backend to relax uniform layout restrictions, and
unifies its uniform buffer handling with the SPIR-V and HLSL backends.

Bug: 448452698

[glsl] Use DecomposeUniformAccess instead of Std140

This prepares the backend to relax uniform layout restrictions, and
unifies its uniform buffer handling with the SPIR-V and HLSL backends.

Bug: 448452698

commit.subject: [spirv] Use DecomposeUniformAccess instead of Std140
commit.message:
[spirv] Use DecomposeUniformAccess instead of Std140

This will allow us to remove the requirement for
`uniformAndStorageBuffer16BitAccess` to enable f16, and prepares the
backend to relax uniform layout restrictions.

Add a special-case for single-element swizzles in the printer, since
the `DecomposeUniformAccess` transform does this.

Bug: 448452698
Fixed: 447407471
Change-Id: Ia54e9295fe745f702d31ca59d4edc0873256367c

commit.subject: [spirv] Use DecomposeUniformAccess instead of Std140
commit.message:
[spirv] Use DecomposeUniformAccess instead of Std140

This will allow us to remove the requirement for
`uniformAndStorageBuffer16BitAccess` to enable f16, and prepares the
backend to relax uniform layout restrictions.

Add a special-case for single-element swizzles in the printer, since
the `DecomposeUniformAccess` transform does this.

Round uniform buffer sizes up to a multiple of 16 bytes in the Vulkan
backend to support the vec4u polyfill.

Suppress a CTS regression that appears to be a pre-existing Mesa bug.

Suppress a whitebox Vulkan test on Mali due to an flaky failure caused
by the rounding up of buffer sizes.

Put this change behind a feature flag (enabled by default), so that we
can killswitch it if something goes wrong in production. Add a toggle
as well so that we can test the fallback path and so that we can
detect the feature for relaxing f16 requirements.

Bug: 448452698
Fixed: 447407471
Include-Ci-Only-Tests: True
Change-Id: Ia54e9295fe745f702d31ca59d4edc0873256367c

commit.subject: Cleans up DEPS
commit.message:
Cleans up DEPS

Cleans up several aspects of Dawn's DEPS file. Specifically:
1. Updates the buildtools/* entries to match Chromium's
2. Updates the third_party/jsoncpp entry to use the Chromium mirror
   instead of Github
3. Actually defines build_with_chromium and uses it as suggested in
   crbug.com/397754746. Additionally, the build override for this is
   removed in favor of exporting it directly from gclient, making the
   DEPS file the single source of truth.

These should all effectively be no-ops.

Bug: 397754746, 452840620
Change-Id: Ie6079251878e7631fa286d096e09ea607e2c94a0

commit.subject: [cmake] Always enable vptr sanitizer
commit.message:
[cmake] Always enable vptr sanitizer

- Older versions of Clang enabled this by default, which caused a build
  incompatibility with Skia. //build also enables it by default in GN,
  so this makes CMake match more closely.
- Fix RTTI flags so this actually works.
- Document why we have float-divide-by-zero sanitizer since we might not
  actually want it.

Bug: 452389542, b:434977307
Change-Id: Ifcdbe04a3588db3543ac269d53471ce561551b20

commit.subject: [cmake] Disable vptr sanitizer on old Clang
commit.message:
[cmake] Disable vptr sanitizer on old Clang

The vptr sanitizer is enabled by -fsanitize=undefined only on older
versions of Clang. We want to enable it (GN enables it along with
is_ubsan), but tint_unittests fails with the version of Clang on our
Linux CMake bots (19.0.0 - perhaps a buggy old version).

tint_unittests passes locally on my machine with Clang 19.1.7, so gate
the vptr sanitizer on that version. Verified locally that the check
controls the flag as expected.

Whenever the bots' Clang gets upgraded, the sanitizer will turn back on
automatically. Or, using a hermetic toolchain (like HermeticXcode.cmake
but for Linux) would also fix it, but it's difficult to set up.

Additionally:
- Fix one more missing RTTI flag control.
- Document why we have the float-divide-by-zero sanitizer, since GN
  doesn't.

Bug: 452389542, b:434977307
Cq-Include-Trybots: luci.dawn.try:cmake-linux-clang-dbg-x64-ubsan,cmake-linux-clang-rel-x64-ubsan
Change-Id: Ifcdbe04a3588db3543ac269d53471ce561551b20

commit.subject: Reland "[dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly."
commit.message:
Reland "[dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly."

This is a reland of commit 11b115b26569c8aa46781b4dac589ce17f5d6c89

Original change's description:
> [dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly.
>
> - With the changes to make the wire more spontaneous, chunked
>   command serialization and handling need to be updated to work
>   in a multithreaded manner. Previously, the handler assumes that
>   once a chunked command is received, it will receive the entire
>   chunked command before it receives any other commands. This may
>   no longer be true, so we upgrade chunked commands into its own
>   command so with unique id's to ensure that we handle them
>   appropriately.
> - This change also unifies the command id enums in the wire to a
>   single enum since chunked command handling may occur on both
>   the server and the client (though in practice in Chromium,
>   only the server->client may be multithreaded for now.) This
>   allows us to handle commands in a unified way and also ensures
>   that the command ids are now unique both direction.
>
> Bug: 412761856
> Change-Id: Ia1eb34d57c2e2fe0457c70aae9348bc051fce573
> Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/266475
> Reviewed-by: Corentin Wallez <cwallez@chromium.org>
> Reviewed-by: Kai Ninomiya <kainino@chromium.org>
> Commit-Queue: Loko Kung <lokokung@google.com>

Bug: 412761856
Change-Id: Ie9c6554908597362cc2576182e09bf49fc35a4b9

commit.subject: Revert "[dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly."
commit.message:
Revert "[dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly."

This reverts commit 11b115b26569c8aa46781b4dac589ce17f5d6c89.

Reason for revert: Fuzzer crash https://crbug.com/452575709

Original change's description:
> [dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly.
>
> - With the changes to make the wire more spontaneous, chunked
>   command serialization and handling need to be updated to work
>   in a multithreaded manner. Previously, the handler assumes that
>   once a chunked command is received, it will receive the entire
>   chunked command before it receives any other commands. This may
>   no longer be true, so we upgrade chunked commands into its own
>   command so with unique id's to ensure that we handle them
>   appropriately.
> - This change also unifies the command id enums in the wire to a
>   single enum since chunked command handling may occur on both
>   the server and the client (though in practice in Chromium,
>   only the server->client may be multithreaded for now.) This
>   allows us to handle commands in a unified way and also ensures
>   that the command ids are now unique both direction.
>
> Bug: 412761856
> Change-Id: Ia1eb34d57c2e2fe0457c70aae9348bc051fce573

commit.subject: Revert "[dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly."
commit.message:
Revert "[dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly."

This reverts commit 11b115b26569c8aa46781b4dac589ce17f5d6c89.

Reason for revert: Fuzzer crash https://crbug.com/452575709

Original change's description:
> [dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly.
>
> - With the changes to make the wire more spontaneous, chunked
>   command serialization and handling need to be updated to work
>   in a multithreaded manner. Previously, the handler assumes that
>   once a chunked command is received, it will receive the entire
>   chunked command before it receives any other commands. This may
>   no longer be true, so we upgrade chunked commands into its own
>   command so with unique id's to ensure that we handle them
>   appropriately.
> - This change also unifies the command id enums in the wire to a
>   single enum since chunked command handling may occur on both
>   the server and the client (though in practice in Chromium,
>   only the server->client may be multithreaded for now.) This
>   allows us to handle commands in a unified way and also ensures
>   that the command ids are now unique both direction.
>
> Bug: 412761856
> Change-Id: Ia1eb34d57c2e2fe0457c70aae9348bc051fce573

commit.subject: Add KDocs to Kotlin bindings from webgpu.yml.
commit.message:
Add KDocs to Kotlin bindings from webgpu.yml.

This change leverages the existing API documentation found in
`webgpu.yml` and adds it into the generated `*.kt` files.

Key Changes:
- Modifying `dawn_json_generator.py` to load and parse the `webgpu.yml` file.
- Created dawn_utility.py to add common utility functions
- Updating the `art_kotlin_enum` template to read the parsed documentation and use it as KDocs for classes, methods, and parameters.

Change-Id: Ia7061962ea926a04f6d788ad16f2992791b0f7ed

commit.subject: [dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly.
commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Handle command chunking in the wire in more robustly.

- With the changes to make the wire more spontaneous, chunked
  command serialization and handling need to be updated to work
  in a multithreaded manner. Previously, the handler assumes that
  once a chunked command is received, it will receive the entire
  chunked command before it receives any other commands. This may
  no longer be true, so we upgrade chunked commands into its own
  command so with unique id's to ensure that we handle them
  appropriately.
- This change also unifies the command id enums in the wire to a
  single enum since chunked command handling may occur on both
  the server and the client (though in practice in Chromium,
  only the server->client may be multithreaded for now.) This
  allows us to handle commands in a unified way and also ensures
  that the command ids are now unique both direction.

Bug: 412761856
Change-Id: Ia1eb34d57c2e2fe0457c70aae9348bc051fce573

commit.subject: EGL: workaround an EGL 1.5 bug in PowerVR drivers.
commit.message:
EGL: workaround an EGL 1.5 bug in PowerVR drivers.

PowerVR drivers claim to support EGL 1.5, but don't support the
EGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_ROBUST_ACCESS enum in the promoted feature. Use the
EGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_ROBUST_ACCESS_EXT enum instead.

Bug: 441938383

commit.message:
EGL: workaround an EGL 1.5 bug in PowerVR drivers.

PowerVR drivers claim to support EGL 1.5, but don't support the
EGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_ROBUST_ACCESS enum in the promoted feature. Use the
EGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_ROBUST_ACCESS_EXT enum instead.

commit.subject: [dawn][wire] Make the server logging callback flush immediately.
commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Make the server logging callback flush immediately.

- With some incoming changes on Chromium side, it becomes necessary
  to force a flush after the logging callbacks because there is an
  expectation that when a thread calls |GetCmdSpace|, that at some point,
  that thread must also call |Flush|. Since the logging callback can
  theoretically be called from anywhere, we need it to also flush to
  ensure that we don't have a thread that calls |GetCmdSpace| that
  never ends up calling |Flush|.

Bug: 412761856
Change-Id: I9c913723e8c5ed9b33d062a0767401ff9496d876

commit.message:
[glsl] Use RemoveUniformVectorComponentLoads

Make the transform a generic transform instead of just for SPIR-V.

We also need to capture the `load` result in a `let`, otherwise the
expression will be inlined and the GLSL compiler will treat it as a
reference.

commit.subject: D3D12: Support creating host mapped buffer with file handle
commit.message:
D3D12: Support creating host mapped buffer with file handle

This patch implements the feature `HostMappedFileHandle` that allows
importing a `HANDLE` of a named shared memory object as a host mapped
buffer on D3D12 backends with `OpenExistingHeapFromFileMapping()`.

Note that an `E_INVALIDARG` will be returned when we use a file handle
in `OpenExistingHeapFromFileMapping()`.

Bug: 42240963
Test: dawn_end2end_tests
Change-Id: I4656a06cb9bc3469f3c42b74edc27217f56ea3f8

commit.subject: [spirv] Add transform to replace uniform vector component loads
commit.message:
[spirv] Add transform to replace uniform vector component loads

Qualcomm devices have a bug that affects pointers into vector
components for large uniform buffers. Remove these by loading the
whole vector and then extracting the component we need.

Add a Dawn E2E test that covers the bug. This is suppressed on the
OpenGLES backend for now as Qualcomm have the same issue in their GLSL
flow.

Bug: 452350626
Change-Id: I0718311ad1f478b6255d344befd3c790da81bd69

commit.message:
vulkan: Prefer HOST_CACHED for mappable GPU buffers

Change the memory type selection logic for BufferMapExtendedUsages
buffers so that it prefers HOST_CACHED for read only buffers instead of
HOST_COHERENT. Also only prefer HOST_CACHED+HOST_COHERENT if the buffer
is both read and write.

commit.subject: vulkan: Change mappable buffer memory selection logic.
commit.message:
vulkan: Change mappable buffer memory selection logic.

For BufferMapExtendedUsages buffers that are read mappable make it
prefer HOST_CACHED for instead of HOST_COHERENT. This matches the logic
for mappable non-device local buffers already.

For BufferMapExtendedUsages buffers that are write mappable make it
prefer HOST_COHERENT over HOST_COHERENT+HOST_CACHED. This is based on
ARM guidance from [1] and the fact that HOST_CACHED might have overhead
but can't help if there is no CPU read access.

For read+write mappable buffers they still prefer
HOST_COHERENT+HOST_CACHED. If a memory type with both is not available
they will now prefer HOST_CACHED memory over HOST_COHERENT memory.

[1] https://developer.arm.com/documentation/101897/0304/CPU-overheads/Vulkan-CPU-memory-mapping

Bug: 422798184
Change-Id: I2727ad64a3f804257aa74c203ada9ddf3209ffff

commit.message:
vulkan: Change mappable buffer memory selection logic

For BufferMapExtendedUsages buffers that are read mappable make it
prefer HOST_CACHED for instead of HOST_COHERENT. This matches the logic
for mappable non-device local buffers already.

For BufferMapExtendedUsages buffers that are write mappable make it
prefer HOST_COHERENT over HOST_COHERENT+HOST_CACHED. This is based on

For read+write mappable buffers they still prefer
HOST_COHERENT+HOST_CACHED. If a memory type with both is not available

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Validate that only pinned usages are allowed.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Validate that only pinned usages are allowed.

When a texture is pinned it cannot be used as any other usage as it
would break the invariant that pinned textures have the correct memory
barriers done without any extra work. This validation was previously
left as a TODO.

Adds tests and also removes the ASSERT in the Vulkan backend that was
trying to catche incorrect use of pinned textures.

Bug: 435317394
Change-Id: I042b981506690e34908dffb822f8a790d7f7b5f1

commit.subject: Change Device::CopyFromStagingToTextureImpl signature
commit.message:
Change Device::CopyFromStagingToTextureImpl signature

Remove "const" keyword from BufferBase* src argument. The caller
CopyFromStagingToTexture() receives non-const BufferBase*, hence there
is no point in passing const pointer to the "Impl" function. It would
restrict the backend from increasing the ref count to keep the src
buffer alive for some deferred operations.

Bug: 451928481
Change-Id: I65ceccffa78148481292ed47900967c38a6e4290

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Factor the logic to compute the tint::Bindings
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Factor the logic to compute the tint::Bindings

This option passed to Tint compilation is used to remap bindings from
WGSL bind points, to whatever the backend needs to match how it sets
BindGroups. The logic in all backends look extremely similar apart from
how they map a (group, index) to a tint::BindPoint.

The logic is extracted in a GenerateBindingRemapping helper function in
TintUtils that takes a backend-specified functor for the mapping of a
(group, index) to a tint::BindPoint.

In the Vulkan backend, some leftover logic for static samplers is
extracted from the generation of the tint::Bindings to modify it a
posteriori.

Bug: 447157265
Change-Id: Ib128c83e71a4ef1916fbe3e1c9475b5f1b680566

commit.subject: [tint] Replace tint::Slice with std::span
commit.message:
[tint] Replace tint::Slice with std::span

This change eliminates the custom tint::Slice type in favor of the
standard C++ std::span, improving code safety and reducing reliance
on unsafe buffer patterns.

Key changes:

1. Updated IR infrastructure:
   - Modified method return types from Slice<T> to std::span<T> in:
     * core::ir::Access::Indices()
     * core::ir::BreakIf::NextIterValues() and ExitValues()
     * core::ir::Call::Args()
     * core::ir::Terminator::Args()

2. Added std::span support to container utilities:
   - Vector<T, N> now supports construction from std::span<T>
   - Transform() function now accepts std::span<T> arguments
   - CloneContext::Clone() and Remap() support std::span<T>
   - Added ToVector() helper for std::span conversion

3. Updated intrinsic table data structures:
   - Changed TableData struct members from Slice<T> to std::span<T>
   - Replaced Empty constant with {} in intrinsic data files across
     all backends (GLSL, HLSL, MSL, SPIR-V)

4. API migration throughout the codebase:
   - Slice::Length() → std::span::size()
   - Slice::Offset(n) → std::span::subspan(n)
   - Slice::Truncate(n) → std::span::subspan(0, n)
   - Slice::Back() → std::span::back()
   - Slice::Front() → std::span::front()
   - Slice::IsEmpty() → std::span::empty()

5. Updated files across multiple subsystems:
   - Core IR and validators
   - GLSL writer
   - HLSL writer
   - MSL writer
   - SPIR-V reader/writer
   - WGSL writer
   - Test files for all affected components

Bug: chromium:449980071

[tint] Replace tint::Slice with std::span /2

This change eliminates the custom tint::Slice type in favor of the
standard C++ std::span, improving code safety and reducing reliance
on unsafe buffer patterns.

Also fix RemoveTerminatorArgs to reset num_next_iter_values_ before
clearing operands, preventing std::span::subspan() out-of-bounds access
during validation.

This should test Emdawnwebgpu build/link on CQ.
To build the bindings and tests locally, build 'emdawnwebgpu'.

- Add GN rules for tests (skipping InitOnlySample which is just for
  manually testing code size).
- Make top-level BUILD.gn rules build these tests when dawn_wasm (not
  is_wasm) is true, so they build whenever Emscripten is available.
  Using is_wasm at the top level would only work if the the default
  toolchain were Emscripten, but that isn't allowed.
- Don't bother to run the few generation targets without Emscripten,
  that was only so they would run on CQ before we had Emscripten
  toolchain support.
- Fix warnings that the GN build catches.
- Unrelated autoformat in //BUILD.gn (dxc:dxc -> dxc).

Verified the tests run locally in debug and release builds.

Verified that the link test builds on CQ by dry running with a missing
symbol in the JS file:
https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/266016/3?checksPatchset=3&tab=checks
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/dawn/builders/try/dawn-cq-mac-x64-rel/331/overview

commit.message:
Add legacy ASAN/UBSAN trybots

Adds manual-only trybots for legacy ASAN/UBSAN builders. Previously, we
omitted a CQ verifier definition for ASAN/UBSAN builders, which resulted
in them not having a trybot mirror at all. Now, we create a version that
is includable-only in such cases.

Bug: 451652368

commit.subject: Allow RTTI to be enabled in the cmake build
commit.message:
Allow RTTI to be enabled in the cmake build

I ran into a problem when Skia was running a UBSAN build that
linked in Dawn built with CMake. We'd see run-time crashes like
    ..._functional/function.h:377:17: runtime error: member call on address 0x00016bd88420 which does not point to an object of type ...
    note: object has invalid vptr

The root cause was that -fsanitizer=vptr (which is enabled by
default when -fsanitizer=undefined is set) requires RTTI (Run-Time
Type Information) to work [1]. When Skia builds with UBSAN (which
is combined with our ASAN build), it enables rtti [2] for
this reason.

Either Skia needs to disable the vptr sanitizer or Dawn's cmake
build needs to be configurable. This is the latter option and
I also have Dawn feed the enable RTTI part to SPIRV [3] to compile
all of Dawn and its dependencies with RTTI. I tested this
locally with Skia's GN->CMake system [4] and it seems to build
and run. There might be more third_party deps to configure beyond
these, but it was hard for me to tell for sure.

[1] https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.html
```
-fsanitize=vptr: ... Incompatible with -fno-rtti.
[2] https://skia.googlesource.com/skia/+/351920c5c618bc14b97e588942c596f3e9313b0e/gn/skia/BUILD.gn#681
[3] https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools/blob/b9997dafc791634ce51f6bed7ab886ea0e600a15/CMakeLists.txt#L48
[4] https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/1037096

Change-Id: Ie56c1efb64f6a8849aeae61f4ec3b33246f83a4d

Add a comment to explain why the assert in ~Result

AFAICT, if you have a ResultOrError and you ignore the result
then you get this assert. It took a while to figure that out

```
ResultOrError<int> foo() { ... }

...

    DAWN_TRY(foo());  // assets because result was ignored
```

commit.message:
[WebGPU Backend] Implement CopyFromStagingTo*

The source buffer is a staging buffer and its mapped pointer is
always accessible regardless of the buffer state is mapped or not.
Simply get data from the mapped pointer and call queueWriteBuffer
or queueWriteTexture.

Turn on some tests.

Fix setting of depth/stencil LoadOp/StoreOp.

commit.subject: [metal] Implement CommandBufferScheduledWaiter callable
commit.message:
[metal] Implement CommandBufferScheduledWaiter callable

We need a thread-safe way to call waitUntilScheduled for a Dawn device
for DrDC + Graphite on Mac. The existing WaitForCommandsToBeScheduled()
method isn't thread-safe if the implicit_device_synchronization feature
is not enabled for the Dawn device e.g. for WebGPU. We can leverage the
fact that the underlying [MTLCommandBuffer waitUntilScheduled] call is
thread-safe and return an Objective-C block that captures the command
buffer to the client which can then later invoke it on any thread.

Bug: chromium:444702048
Change-Id: Icd97c05d6274d5cf9f607a0019e1d9ec6a6a6964

commit.subject: [metal] Implement commands scheduled future
commit.message:
[metal] Implement commands scheduled future

We need a thread-safe way to call waitUntilScheduled for a Dawn device
for DrDC + Graphite on Mac. The existing WaitForCommandsToBeScheduled()
method isn't thread-safe if the implicit_device_synchronization feature
is not enabled for the Dawn device e.g. for WebGPU.

This CL adds a `SharedTextureMemoryMetalEndAccessState` extension struct
that contains a `commandsScheduledFuture`. This future is ready when
the Metal command buffer submitted on `EndAccess` is in scheduled state.
This future can be waited on any thread with wgpu::Instance::WaitAny.

Bug: chromium:444702048
Change-Id: Icd97c05d6274d5cf9f607a0019e1d9ec6a6a6964

commit.subject: Add a Reset() method to RefBase.
commit.message:
Add a Reset() method to RefBase.

It's convenient to have a Reset() method on RefBase in cases where
calling operator=(nullptr_t) is not possible e.g. when your RefBase is
wrapped in another smart-pointer-like type like a MutexProtected's
Guard where it can only access regular methods via operator-> chaining.

This CL also adds missing(?) tests for assignment to nullptr and the new
Reset() method both of which behave exactly the same way.

Bug: chromium:444702048
Change-Id: Icd97c05d6274d5cf9f607a0019e1d9ec6a6a6964

commit.subject: [metal] Implement commands scheduled future
commit.message:
[metal] Implement commands scheduled future

We need a thread-safe way to call waitUntilScheduled for a Dawn device
for DrDC + Graphite on Mac. The existing WaitForCommandsToBeScheduled()
method isn't thread-safe if the implicit_device_synchronization feature
is not enabled for the Dawn device e.g. for WebGPU.

This CL adds a `SharedTextureMemoryMetalEndAccessState` extension struct
that contains a `commandsScheduledFuture`. This future is ready when
the Metal command buffer submitted on `EndAccess` is in scheduled state.
This future can be waited on any thread with wgpu::Instance::WaitAny.

Bug: chromium:444702048
Change-Id: Iffa3d773822185add0da96e9101f4aa46a6a6964

commit.subject: Add a Reset() method to RefBase.
commit.message:
Add a Reset() method to RefBase.

It's convenient to have a Reset() method on RefBase in cases where
calling operator=(nullptr_t) is not possible e.g. when your RefBase is
wrapped in another smart-pointer-like type like a MutexProtected's
Guard where it can only access regular methods via operator-> chaining.
It's also idiomatic in C++ for smart pointer types to have a reset
method even if they also have a similar operator=(nullptr_t).

This CL also adds missing(?) tests for assignment to nullptr and the new
Reset() method both of which behave exactly the same way.

Bug: chromium:444702048
Change-Id: Iffa3d773822185add0da96e9101f4aa46a6a6964

commit.subject: Move texture component swizzle usage restrictions
commit.message:
Move texture component swizzle usage restrictions

In the current texture swizzle proposal, a non-default swizzle is not
allowed on a texture view that has usage RENDER_ATTACHMENT or
STORAGE_BINDING. This CL changes it so that:
- a view passed as a colorAttachment or depthStencilAttachment or

commit.subject: [tint] Replace tint::Slice with std::span /1
commit.message:
[tint] Replace tint::Slice with std::span /1

This is the first of a number of patches that replace using
tint::Slice with std::span, where span is a drop in replacement. It
also adds AsSpan() to tint::Vector to make it slight more ergonomic to
get a span of a vector.

The specific locations updated in this CL:
- the IR fuzzer
- IR binary decoding
- the WGSL fuzzer
- roundtrip fuzzing
- bytes BufferReader

Bug: 449980071

Change-Id: Ib9803a01e18ed7dfe8b2234053c8f6b1acbe3da5

commit.subject: Avoid use-after-move in Blob.h
commit.message:
Avoid use-after-move in Blob.h

I noticed some interesting crashes [1] when working on an unrelated
task. Gemini pointed out that it's probably not a good idea to hold onto
vec's data pointer after we've moved it. While much of the time the new
vector might take over the underlying pointer, this won't work if the
vector implementation uses Small Vector Optimization (SVO). In that case
vec.data() would be pointing to the stack and then after the move (which
copies the stack data to the heap) the pointer is invalid.

By grabbing the data and size from the moved vector, we'll avoid the
invalid pointer.

[1]
https://logs.chromium.org/logs/skia/73de020340d43911/+/steps/dm/0/stdout

Change-Id: I3548d2c414a43ad0388996466496e1644f3eef67

commit.subject: Fix incorrect continue target.
commit.message:
Fix incorrect continue target.

A single-block loop inside the continuing of a parent loop may have the
continuing block as it's continuing target. Previously we'd set the
outer loop as the continue target in the IR which is invalid. Instead,
when we're emitting the continue block, remove the continuing
information so it can be re-added when we emit the inner loop.

Fixed: 42250521
Change-Id: I77c4fe115008eee6c68ed9c20131d89a573d85c4

commit.subject: Fix intrinsic match for spirv intrinsics.
commit.message:
Fix intrinsic match for spirv intrinsics.

For the `image` and `sampled_image` intrinsics they are renamed to have
an `op_` prefix to differentiate them from the equivalent types and the
images are moved to be explicit template parameters. This fixes the
matching algorithm failing to match when they're implicit.

Fixed: 448679392
Change-Id: I718952c614071863148ee8669ad7c4c0265eca34

commit.subject: Add gn_v2 ClusterFuzz corpora generator
commit.message:
Add gn_v2 ClusterFuzz corpora generator

Adds dawn-linux-x64-sws-clusterfuzz, which is the gn_v2 equivalent of
cron-linux-clang-rel-x64. No trybot mirror is added since this is
intended to only ever run on CI. As such, tests are also enabled as
part of this CL.

Tests still use the no-op merge script for now since the merge script
for uploading ClusterFuzz corpora will need to be updated to support
both gtests and isolated scripts. This should still allow us to confirm
that tests run correctly and that they output the expected trace data.

commit.subject: Allow ErrorScope resolution to block on AsyncTasks
commit.message:
Allow ErrorScope resolution to block on AsyncTasks

Store a list of pending async tasks in error scopes. These tasks are
gathered during PopErrorScope and a WaitListEvent is used to wait until
they are all complete before the PopErrorScope future is marked
complete.

It is not always known which types of errors will be generated by an
AsyncTask so it may write to different error scopes. To handle this, the
AsyncTasks are associated with multiple error scopes with a filter on
which type of error should be handled.

Add a new child class ErrorGeneratingAsyncTask to wrap tasks which
return MaybeError.

commit.subject: Reland "Explicitly list Go architectures"
commit.message:
Reland "Explicitly list Go architectures"

This is a reland of commit 455fc163a6e844c39aca00cab96f37ac71024f8b

Original change's description:
> Explicitly list Go architectures
>
> Updates Dawn's Go dependency to explicitly fetch CIPD packages for all
> supported architectures for an OS instead of relying on ${{platform}}.
> Known users of this dependency are also updated to select the correct
> copy based on the OS/arch combination at runtime. However, since the old
> files are not automatically removed, it is possible that things may
> break at a later point when the builder cache is cleared if a user of Go
> was missed.
>
> This is necessary in order to properly support running tests which use
> the Go code under //tools/src on OSes that support multiple
> architectures. Using ${{platform}} when fetching dependencies implicitly
> assumes that the architecture of the machine fetching dependencies is
> the same as the machine that will run tests. This assumption does not
> hold true now that we support running tests on Swarming, as Mac in
> particular prefers to build on arm64 regardless of which architecture is
> being built for.
>
> Bug: 441328362
> Change-Id: I8829b17f31d7604e1e494e99cc50fd257484c9e1
> Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/264976
> Auto-Submit: Brian Sheedy <bsheedy@google.com>
> Commit-Queue: Kai Ninomiya <kainino@chromium.org>

commit.subject: Update gn_v2 MSVC GN args and tests
commit.message:
Update gn_v2 MSVC GN args and tests

Updates the gn_v2 MSVC builder to build non-component builds without
SwiftShader. The compile failures we have been seeing are caused by
building the `default` target with component builds.

SwiftShader may run into issues on non-component builds due to frequent
loading/unloading of the library. We will see if Dawn tests run into
any such issues, and if so, `dawn_use_swiftshader` will be disabled
and relevant tests removed in a follow-up.

Bug: 385317083
Change-Id: Ic35c19b915450310dddb1a3cdb2c97619ca15039

commit.subject: Update wrapper script args
commit.message:
Update wrapper script args

Adds the following unused args to run_dawn_node_cts.py and
run_tint_fuzzer_corpus_tests.py:

* --isolated-script-test-launcher-retry-limit
* --isolated-script-test-repeat
* --isolated-script-test-filter

These are currently unused, but need to be parsed in the Python wrapper
so that they are not forwarded on to the underlying Go runner. Without
this, it is possible for infra regressions to make it past the CQ like
in https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/dawn/builders/try/dawn-cq-linux-x64-fuzz-rel/713/infra

Order of events that happened there:

1. Tests failed due to an issue introduced by the CL
2. Builder retried tests without the CL applied in order to check if the
   failure is the CL's fault. In order to account for possible
   flakiness, extra args are passed in such as
   --isolated-script-test-repeat=10
3. Tests also fail without the CL applied because the Go code receives
   an unknown argument.
4. Builder exonerates the CL of the test failures

Bug: 441328362, 441327468
Change-Id: If83e357e5cdd4b9a33acacd3191629cb77796ea0

commit.subject: Validate padding size.
commit.message:
Validate padding size.

In order to fix issues in backends, limit the padding size allowed in
structures. The GLSL backend ends up emitting a structure member for
each set of padding bytes, when there is megabytes of padding, this is a
lot of members to emit and causes timeouts.

As a first pass, allow 10meg of padding to be inserted as a maximum
between structure members.

Fixed: 415096334
Change-Id: I5d18dbaa2bb11b3861a170ef114492668da7ee8f

commit.subject: Revert "Explicitly list Go architectures"
commit.message:
Revert "Explicitly list Go architectures"

This reverts commit 455fc163a6e844c39aca00cab96f37ac71024f8b.

Reason for revert: Breaks fuzz builders

Original change's description:
> Explicitly list Go architectures
>
> Updates Dawn's Go dependency to explicitly fetch CIPD packages for all
> supported architectures for an OS instead of relying on ${{platform}}.
> Known users of this dependency are also updated to select the correct
> copy based on the OS/arch combination at runtime. However, since the old
> files are not automatically removed, it is possible that things may
> break at a later point when the builder cache is cleared if a user of Go
> was missed.
>
> This is necessary in order to properly support running tests which use
> the Go code under //tools/src on OSes that support multiple
> architectures. Using ${{platform}} when fetching dependencies implicitly
> assumes that the architecture of the machine fetching dependencies is
> the same as the machine that will run tests. This assumption does not
> hold true now that we support running tests on Swarming, as Mac in
> particular prefers to build on arm64 regardless of which architecture is
> being built for.
>

commit.subject: Explicitly list Go architectures
commit.message:
Explicitly list Go architectures

Updates Dawn's Go dependency to explicitly fetch CIPD packages for all
supported architectures for an OS instead of relying on ${{platform}}.
Known users of this dependency are also updated to select the correct
copy based on the OS/arch combination at runtime. However, since the old
files are not automatically removed, it is possible that things may
break at a later point when the builder cache is cleared if a user of Go
was missed.

This is necessary in order to properly support running tests which use
the Go code under //tools/src on OSes that support multiple
architectures. Using ${{platform}} when fetching dependencies implicitly
assumes that the architecture of the machine fetching dependencies is
the same as the machine that will run tests. This assumption does not
hold true now that we support running tests on Swarming, as Mac in
particular prefers to build on arm64 regardless of which architecture is
being built for.

Bug: 441328362
Change-Id: I8829b17f31d7604e1e494e99cc50fd257484c9e1
